summary: A short notice that the network graphics meeting planned for October 17 to 19, 1971 at Stanford AI would be postponed because it clashed with the Network Working Group meeting. A new date would be announced later, probably in November or December.

today: RFC 232 is a brief administrative notice from the early ARPANET era. It reflects the growing coordination required as the network community expanded its meetings and working groups.

sections.title: Meeting Postponement
sections.content: RFC 232 is a short notice that the Network Graphics meeting, tentatively scheduled for October 17, 18, and 19, 1971 at Stanford AI, has been postponed. The reason is a scheduling conflict: the Network Working Group meeting is being held October 10-14, making back-to-back meetings impractical.
sections.eli5: Two different meetings were planned for the same week, so one had to move.

sections.title: New Schedule
sections.content: A new date for the Network Graphics meeting will be established and announced via RFC. The meeting is expected to be held in the San Francisco area in November or early December 1971.
sections.eli5: A new date will be picked and announced later.

sections.title: Background
sections.content: The Network Graphics meeting was tentatively scheduled following the July 1971 meeting at MIT. The decision to postpone came after the October Network Working Group meeting dates were finalized, creating a scheduling conflict.
sections.eli5: The two communities planned meetings on the same dates without realizing it until it was too late to change.
